content:
Thunderbird is an email client. It connects to your Email Service Provider ( for Example Gmail ) that you choose to use and downloads email from Gmail to Thunderbird on your device ( PC, Smart Phone ).

There are 2 types for connections or Server : IMAP and POP.

When IMAP is configured "everything" that you do to your emails with Thunderbird will be synchronized to your Gmail server and Vice versa. Example if you delete an email of your Gmail account using Thunderbird, that email will also be deleted from Gmail server. If you delete an email from your Gmail account using web browser, that same email will also be deleted from Thunderbird locally.

If you don't want that type of synchronization then you should choose POP server ( or Connection ).

To have more details I suggest that take a look at :

https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/products/thunderbird https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/products/thunderbird/settings https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/imap-synchronization https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/difference-between-imap-and-pop3

content:
Over 3G of memory for a small profile size is a lot according to my opinion ( I might be wrong ).

If you don't backup your profile regularly, I would suggest that you backup your profile before going further.

To backup Thunderbird profile : shutdown Thunderbird and then backup all files and subdirectories of the profile directory

Create 2 new profile lets call it PT01 and PT02 ( as for reference of this "conversation" ) ( https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/profile-manager-create-and-remove-thunderbird-profiles#w_creating-a-profile )

Now start thunderbird using this new "empty" profile PT01, don't add any account to it. Go to Settings and look at different parameters ( for example go to General, up and down, ) in General, Appearance etc, go to help look at Troubleshooting information, and browse ....  : the purpose of this step is to see if Thunderbird is leaking memory ( without any account added ) and is it easy to use. Please verify memory usage during your "browsing" in Thunderbird settings .

Now start Thunderbird using new empty profile PT02. Now you add only 1 account ( if you have more than one ). I don't know if you using IMAP or POP, for this test purpose I would suggest to use IMAP ( because POP would downloads emails and delete some emails depending on your configuration to your PT02 ). The only thing you would do is this account is browsing different emails and at most send some "test emails". The purpose of this step is to see if this account would trigger memory leak. If there is no memory leak than add another account ( if you had more ).

Let try this and then we'll see if you agree.
